modern: Never value anything as profitable to yourself which will force you to break your promise, to lose your self-respect, to hate any man, to suspect, to curse, to act the hypocrite, to desire anything which needs walls and curtains: for he who has preferred his own intelligence and the spirit within, and the worship of its excellence, to everything else, plays no tragic part, does not groan, and will need neither solitude nor much company; and, most important of all, he will live without either pursuing death or fleeing from it; and whether his soul is to be enclosed in the body for a longer or a shorter time, he does not care at all: for even if he must depart immediately, he will go as readily as if he were going to do anything else which can be done with decency and order; taking care of this only, all through life, that his thoughts do not turn away from anything which belongs to an intelligent animal and a member of a civic community.
